name: Final grade
seoDesc: Final grade: answer 129 values and the page computes the result when you press Calculate — formula and worked example included.
summary:
The Final grade calculator is a free, no-sign-up other tool. Fill in the 108 fields it asks for and it works out the answer straight away, with the formula shown underneath.

It is built for whatever you happen to be working on. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Final grade calculator work?
sections.html:
The Final grade calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the grading System, the you want a final grade of (Your grade(s)) and the you want a final grade of (Your grade(s))); then you type in the you want a final grade of (Your grade(s)), the you want a final grade of (Results) and the you need (Results).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Final grade calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

The final exam is=(your current grade is... − you want a final grade of) ÷ (your current grade is... − you need)
You need=(grading System, you want a final grade of, it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., (-it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... + 1))
Your final exam is worth=(-it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... + 1)
You want a final grade of=100 × you want a final grade of
You need=((grading System, you want a final grade of, it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., it is worth..., your grade was..., (-it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... − it is worth... + 1)))
You need=(you need, grading System)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Final grade calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Final grade calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 108 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter you want a final grade of (Your grade(s)) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. You want a final grade of (Your grade(s)) opens in percent and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (87 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports You want a final grade of = 9825 %. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Final grade calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
